mission_09: Time series anomaly detection requires specialized methods that account for temporal dependencies, trends, and seasonality. Standard outlier detection methods that assume i.i.d. data are inappropriate for time series where consecutive observations are correlated. Rolling Z-score computes the deviation of each point from a rolling window mean, normalized by the rolling standard deviation, adapting to local changes in the data distribution. Seasonal decomposition separates the time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components, with anomalies detected in the residuals. Exponential smoothing provides adaptive forecasts, and large prediction errors indicate anomalies. These methods are essential for monitoring sensor data, financial markets, network traffic, and any temporal data where anomalies manifest as deviations from expected patterns rather than absolute extreme values.
